items.title: Hamstring watch: Whitfield works on the side field
items.text:
The defense spent most of the session on red-zone looks, with the starting secondary rotating in and out as the staff tried a few new pressure packages. The linebackers coach said the group has been sharper in communication this week after a string of busted assignments, and several veterans stayed late to watch film together.

Trey Whitfield worked on a side field with a trainer and ran sprints at what looked like about seventy percent. The staff will make the final decision on him during pregame warmups after seeing how the leg responds to a full-speed workout on the field.

On the offensive line, the right guard returned from a back issue and took his usual reps with the first unit. The left tackle was given a rest day, which the head coach described as routine maintenance for a player in his eleventh season. The backup center continued to take snaps with the second group.

Special teams had a lengthy period focused on punt coverage after last week's return touchdown. The coordinator said he wants more discipline in the lanes and hinted that a couple of younger players could see their roles change. The returner job remains open between two rookies.

The head coach opened his news conference by praising the effort in last week's loss but said the turnovers were unacceptable. He declined to discuss the quarterback situation in detail, saying only that the starter has his full confidence and that the plan for Sunday has not changed.

The head coach opened his news conference by praising the effort in last week's loss but said the turnovers were unacceptable. He declined to discuss the quarterback situation in detail, saying only that the starter has his full confidence and that the plan for Sunday has not changed.

With the coordinator gone, the quarterbacks coach will take over play-calling duties from the booth, and the head coach said the core of the offense will stay the same for the rest of the season.

The tight ends worked on blocking drills early before joining the receivers for seven-on-seven. A rookie tight end drew praise for his hands, catching everything thrown his way, though the staff wants him to improve as an inline blocker before he earns a bigger share of the snaps.

Weather pushed part of the walkthrough indoors, and the team will hold its final full practice on Friday. The injury report will be released after that session, and the coach said he expects most of the roster to be available for the trip.

The defense spent most of the session on red-zone looks, with the starting secondary rotating in and out as the staff tried a few new pressure packages. The linebackers coach said the group has been sharper in communication this week after a string of busted assignments, and several veterans stayed late to watch film together.

Coaches have made Jalen Pryce carry a football with him everywhere in the facility this week, including to meetings and the cafeteria, a drill the running backs coach has used before for players with fumbling issues.

The defense spent most of the session on red-zone looks, with the starting secondary rotating in and out as the staff tried a few new pressure packages. The linebackers coach said the group has been sharper in communication this week after a string of busted assignments, and several veterans stayed late to watch film together.

On the offensive line, the right guard returned from a back issue and took his usual reps with the first unit. The left tackle was given a rest day, which the head coach described as routine maintenance for a player in his eleventh season. The backup center continued to take snaps with the second group.

Cole Haverty's new contract includes forty-five million dollars fully guaranteed at signing and a full no-trade clause, a rare protection for a player at his position.

Special teams had a lengthy period focused on punt coverage after last week's return touchdown. The coordinator said he wants more discipline in the lanes and hinted that a couple of younger players could see their roles change. The returner job remains open between two rookies.
